title: The Call After Nine Years • The First Pause at Dhu al-Hulayfah • The Worn Saddle, the Four-Dirham Cloak • Before the Ka‘bah • For All Time • ‘Ali’s Anger • At ‘Arafah with Everyone • Standing at the Bottom of the Valley • Fear Allah Regarding Women • What Will You Say About Me?

blocks.1: A house in Madinah. Outside, the city has changed a great deal. The Prophet {{1}} is no more. Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthman, ‘Ali; one by one their eras too have passed. New faces in the streets, a new generation. Those who never saw the Prophet {{2}}, but in whose chests a question is awake: what was he like? How did he perform Hajj? Inside the house an old man. Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA). The light of his eyes has gone out. But with these very eyes one day he had seen the Prophet {{3}} on the plain of ‘Arafah, before countless people. That picture still glows within his mind. A group of people came into the house. Among them was Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, then young. The grandson of Husayn, the grandson of the Prophet {{4}}. He had not seen that Hajj. He had come to hear it from the mouth of one who had. The names of the others are not in the narration. The blind Jabir (RA) asked each one in turn who they were. At last the turn came to that young man. He said, I am Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn. The old man stretched out his hand and touched his head. Then he undid the upper button of the shirt, then the lower one. Placing his palm on his chest he said, welcome, nephew, ask whatever you wish. From this one scene the knowledge of the religion has come to us. An eyewitness is speaking, a young man listens with ears open, then the narration passes through the hands of another generation and is written in book after book. Today’s dars too stands at the very last end of that chain. Every word we will hear came from the mouth of an eyewitness Companion. The time of prayer came. Jabir (RA) stood wrapping a small cloak around himself. When put on the shoulder its two ends fell back, so small was it. Beside him another cloak hung on the rack, yet he led the prayer in this one.{{5}}
blocks.2: After the prayer the young man asked, tell me of the Prophet’s {{1}} Hajj. Jabir (RA) counted on the fingers of his hand and showed, nine. Then he said,
blocks.3: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} stayed nine years (in Madinah) without performing Hajj. Then in the tenth year it was announced among the people that the Messenger of Allah {{2}} was going for Hajj. A great number of people came and gathered in Madinah; each wished to follow the Messenger of Allah {{3}}, to act as he acted.{{4}}
blocks.4: The Ka‘bah is free now. The year before, Hajj had been held under the leadership of Abu Bakr (RA) (Dars 24). ‘Ali (RA) had announced at Mina, after this year no polytheist will perform Hajj, and no one will circumambulate naked. To that freed House this time the Prophet {{1}} came himself.{{2}}
blocks.5: Why did so many people rush? Because the design of how the acts of Hajj were to be done was not on paper. There was only one person from whom to learn by watching. Today we too pray, fast, go for Hajj. We have no chance to see him with our own eyes. We have narration spoken from the mouths of people like Jabir, which has reached us changing hands generation after generation. This dars will proceed holding to that narration.
blocks.6: The First Pause at Dhu al-Hulayfah
blocks.7: Departure from Madinah with five nights left of Dhu al-Qa‘dah. ‘A’ishah (RA) says,
blocks.8: We set out with the Messenger of Allah {{1}} with five nights left of Dhu al-Qa‘dah; we were thinking of nothing but Hajj.{{2}}
blocks.9: On reaching Dhu al-Hulayfah, a child was born to Asma’ bint ‘Umays (RA), Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr. Asma’ (RA) sent someone to the Prophet {{1}} to ask, what should I do now? The answer came,
blocks.10: Bathe, bind on a cloth, and enter ihram.{{1}}
blocks.11: A newborn in her lap, bleeding ongoing, yet no door of this journey was closed to her. At the very first stage the answer to her question came, straight, easy, in three acts. However large the crowd in this worship, even the difficulty of one mother after childbirth did not escape the Prophet’s {{1}} ear.
blocks.12: Bathing before entering ihram, and perfume on the body. ‘A’ishah (RA) had applied fragrance to the Prophet {{1}} with her own hands. She says,
blocks.13: It is as though I can still see the gleam of perfume in the parting of the Messenger of Allah’s {{1}} hair, while he was in ihram.{{2}}
blocks.14: The cloth of ihram is plain, but the fragrance before it is part of the Sunnah. Plain does not mean rough. Even in the Hajj of Jahiliyyah there was a talbiyah. But shirk had entered that call. Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) says,
blocks.15: The polytheists used to say, labbayka la sharika lak. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} would say, woe to you, stop, stop! But they would say, illa sharikan huwa lak, tamlikuhu wa-ma malak; that is, except one partner of Yours, whom You own, and what he owns. They would say this while circumambulating the Ka‘bah.{{2}}
blocks.16: Circling around the House of Allah and, in front of Allah Himself, acknowledging a partner! The Prophet {{1}} changed the very words of that call. Cutting off the tail of shirk, he kept only tawhid. Then prayer in the mosque of Dhu al-Hulayfah, and that changed call. Mounting the she-camel al-Qaswa. As the she-camel stood upright on the plain of al-Bayda’, the sound of the talbiyah. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.17: He recited the talbiyah of tawhid: labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa-al-ni‘mata laka wa-al-mulk, la sharika lak.{{1}}
blocks.19: I looked as far as my eye could see. Riders and walkers ahead, the same on the right, the same on the left, the same behind. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} in our midst, the Qur’an being revealed upon him, he alone knows its explanation. Whatever he does, we do too.{{2}}
blocks.20: The words of the talbiyah the Prophet {{1}} had himself fixed, as given above. But some in the caravan were adding to it some words familiar to them. The Prophet {{2}} did not forbid them, but did not give up his own talbiyah either. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.21: The people recited the talbiyah that they recite. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} turned away none of it, and held to his own talbiyah.{{2}}
blocks.22: In most voices the same call, which he himself had taught. He did not turn away the extra words, but held on to his own words. The Sunnah is his words. In the middle one, who sees the Qur’an descending and knows its meaning.{{1}}
blocks.23: On a path we do not know, the safest walking is behind the one who knows the path.
blocks.24: The Worn Saddle, the Four-Dirham Cloak
blocks.25: In the middle of this caravan, he who is there, what is his mount like? Anas (RA) says,
blocks.26: The Prophet {{1}} performed Hajj on a worn saddle, wearing a cloak worth four dirhams or less. Then he said, O Allah, a Hajj in which there is no riya’, no sum‘ah.{{2}}
blocks.27: In the courts of Rome and Persia there were golden thrones then. And in the middle of the greatest gathering of Arabia, he at whose call people had rushed, his mount’s saddle is worn, his cloak is worth four dirhams. And his prayer? A Hajj in which there is nothing to show. We announce before going for Hajj, and on return, photographs. Even on the journey to the House of Allah we look for spectators. His prayer was exactly the opposite.
blocks.29: On reaching Makkah, first the Ka‘bah. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.30: He touched the Rukn (the Black Stone), then performed ramal in three circuits (walked with quick steps), and walked in four circuits.{{1}}
blocks.31: Then Safa. Climbing Safa he looked at the Ka‘bah, facing the qiblah he spoke of Allah’s oneness and greatness. He recited three times, and between them made supplication. Jabir (RA) says, he said,
blocks.32: There is no god but Allah, He is One, He has no partner. His is the kingdom, His is the praise, He has power over all things. There is no god but Allah alone; He has fulfilled His promise, helped His servant, and defeated the (disbelieving) parties by Himself alone.{{1}}
blocks.33: Standing on Safa he spoke of no achievement of his own. The promise is Allah’s, the help is Allah’s, the defeat too is in His hand. One day this city had driven him out. Today, standing on Mount Safa of that very city, the word he said, in its beginning Allah, in its end Allah.
blocks.35: The last circuit of Safa–Marwah. Standing on Marwah the Prophet {{1}} said a word that was not easy for many in the caravan. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.36: If I had known earlier what I came to know later, I would not have brought the sacrificial animal, and would have made this an ‘umrah.{{1}}
blocks.37: Those who have no sacrificial animal with them will undo their ihram, before Hajj. Many of the Companions were hesitating. Undo ihram, everything lawful, then a few days later again the ihram of Hajj. Suraqah ibn Malik (RA) stood up.{{1}}
blocks.38: O Messenger of Allah, is this only for this year, or for all time? The Prophet {{1}} interlaced the fingers of one hand into the fingers of the other and said, ‘umrah has entered into Hajj. He said it twice. Then he said, no, rather for all time, for all time.{{2}}
blocks.39: That in which he himself was bound (he could not undo ihram because he had the sacrificial animal), an easier path than that he opened before others. And he said openly, had I known earlier, I too would have done so. In the mouth of a leader this ‘had I known earlier’ is so rare. To value people’s ease above one’s own decision.
blocks.41: In this very Hajj ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) came from Yemen, bringing sacrificial camels for the Prophet {{1}}. Coming, he saw that Fatimah (RA) had undone her ihram. Coloured clothes on her body, kohl in her eyes. ‘Ali (RA) objected. Fatimah (RA) said, my father has commanded me so. ‘Ali (RA) used to say later in Iraq,
blocks.42: I went to the Messenger of Allah {{1}} angry with Fatimah, to ask for a ruling on what Fatimah had narrated from him. I told him, I am angry with her. He said, she has spoken the truth, she has spoken the truth.{{2}}
blocks.43: Then the Prophet {{1}} asked ‘Ali (RA), what did you say when you made the intention for Hajj? ‘Ali (RA) said, I said, O Allah, with the very intention with which Your Messenger has entered ihram, I too enter. He said, I have the sacrificial animals with me, do not undo your ihram.{{2}}
blocks.44: ‘Ali (RA) did not let the displeasure inside the house gather in the house. He went straight and asked what the truth was. And the testimony that came in answer was for the wife: she has spoken the truth, she has spoken the truth. The same words twice, so there is no doubt. How much easier it is to go up and find out than to pass judgement without knowing which words are true! And how effortlessly those two words from the Prophet’s {{1}} mouth cooled the anger of a house.
blocks.46: The eighth of Dhu al-Hijjah, Yawm al-Tarwiyah. The caravan toward Mina. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.47: When the day of Tarwiyah came they set out toward Mina and entered the ihram of Hajj. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} mounted, and there prayed Zuhr, ‘Asr, Maghrib, ‘Isha’ and Fajr. Then he waited a little until the sun rose, and commanded a tent of hair to be pitched for him at Namirah.{{2}}
blocks.48: The Quraysh believed he would stop at al-Mash‘ar al-Haram at Muzdalifah. The custom of Jahiliyyah: Quraysh and their followers called themselves ‘Hums’ and did not go outside the boundary of the Haram (to ‘Arafah). They would say, we are the dwellers of the Haram. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.49: Quraysh were sure he would stop at al-Mash‘ar al-Haram, as Quraysh used to do in Jahiliyyah. But the Messenger of Allah {{1}} passed beyond there and reached ‘Arafah.{{2}}
blocks.50: Behind this crossing was a command of the Qur’an. Allah had said,
blocks.52: And (remember this also) that you shall set out from the place from which other people set out. And ask forgiveness of Allah. Surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.{{1}}
blocks.53: The Prophet {{1}}, a son of Quraysh. The custom that was the pride of his own tribe, he crossed the line of that custom. And he stood where everyone stands. We too sometimes draw such a line. I am this, they are that. I will stop here, let them go there. The Prophet’s {{2}} way is the way of standing with everyone.
blocks.54: Standing at the Bottom of the Valley
blocks.55: As the sun declined he asked that al-Qaswa be saddled. Then he came down to the bottom of the valley, and gave an address before the people. Jabir (RA) has said in brief,
blocks.56: Then he came to the bottom of the valley and gave an address before the people.{{1}}
blocks.57: The ground is so vast, a voice does not reach. In the narration it is said that Rabi‘ah ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf (RA) was spreading each sentence of the Prophet {{1}} in a loud voice, and the people were passing them on again to one another.{{2}}
blocks.58: The first announcements of the address we saw in the earlier dars. All the customs of Jahiliyyah under the feet (Dars 2), the blood-revenge abolished, first of all the blood of the infant son of Rabi‘ah ibn al-Harith of his own clan (Dars 2), usury abolished, first of all the dues of his own uncle ‘Abbas (Dars 2), and the sanctity of life, wealth and honour (Dars 2). There their roots were looked at, from where inside Jahiliyyah and how they had come. Here comes the rest of the address, and the condition of the man himself who says these things.
blocks.60: The root of this part of the ‘Arafah address we have seen in Dars 2; what he changed in a society that buried daughters in the ground. Now the whole structure of the statement. Jabir (RA) says, he said,
blocks.61: Fear Allah regarding women. You have taken them by the trust of Allah, and made their private parts lawful to yourselves by the word of Allah. Your right over them is that they not let anyone you dislike sit on your bed. If they do, then strike them with a blow that is not painful. And their right over you is to provide their food and clothing in a fair manner.{{1}}
blocks.62: In the first sentence, the fear of Allah. The statement is not of control, but of accountability. Then two pans of the scale: your right, her right. And her right is written in food and clothing, ‘bi-al-ma‘ruf’, that is, fair, by the customary good measure. ‘Amr ibn al-Ahwas (RA) too had heard the address of the Farewell Hajj. In his narration,
blocks.63: Listen, take counsel to treat women well. They are dependants with you; apart from that you do not own anything over them, unless they commit open indecency.{{1}}
blocks.64: And the witness of the house of the one from whose mouth this address came is ‘A’ishah (RA). She says,
blocks.65: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} never struck anything with his own hand, neither a woman nor a servant; except in jihad in the way of Allah.{{2}}
blocks.66: Placing this testimony beside the conditional permission that came in the address completes the picture. The one from whose mouth the words came never in his life laid a hand on any woman. At the moment a hand is raised in a house, the biggest question is therefore this: the one whose words these are, what would he have done?
blocks.67: What Will You Say About Me?
blocks.68: At this point of the address he came to his own words. Until now the talk had been about people’s rights. Now the talk is about himself, and what he is leaving behind. Jabir (RA) says, he said,
blocks.69: I am leaving among you something which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray after this: the Book of Allah. And you will be asked about me. What will you say then? They said, we testify that you conveyed, fulfilled the trust, gave counsel. Then he raised his forefinger toward the sky, and brought it down toward the people, and said, O Allah, be witness. O Allah, be witness. Three times.{{1}}
blocks.70: By speaking of holding fast to the Qur’an, he seemed to settle the account of everything. I will not be here. What I am leaving is the path. And that movement of the finger! Toward the sky, toward the people. Making Allah witness before the people, making the people witness before Allah. The question was to the listeners of that day. But the burden of that testimony is now on our shoulders, we who have heard his narration. The religion he conveyed and left, does my life bear witness to it?

footnotes.0: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA), through Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn; sahih). The longest sahih narration of the Farewell Hajj. Jabir’s blindness, the unbuttoning, prayer in the small cloak: the opening part of the narration (Muslim 1218). The narrator is Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn himself; he tells it to his son Ja‘far ibn Muhammad. In the original text: ‘we entered upon Jabir (dakhalna ‘ala Jabir), he asked the identity of the party until he reached me’. How many were in the party and who they were is not stated in the narration; only Muhammad is called ‘young’ (ghulamun shabbun).
footnotes.1: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA); sahih). ‘Nine years’ counted from the hijrah; Jabir shows nine by counting on his fingers.
footnotes.2: Sahih al-Bukhari 369, 4655, 4656 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA); sahih). The incident is in detail in the section ‘Abu Bakr, Amir of Hajj’ of Dars 24.
footnotes.3: Sahih al-Bukhari 1709 (from ‘A’ishah (RA); sahih). Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 748 (sirah-based): departure on Saturday, 25 Dhu al-Qa‘dah, after Zuhr; Dhu al-Hulayfah before ‘Asr. The date and day are not in the sahih hadith, so they have not been put in the narration.
footnotes.5: Sahih Muslim 1190 (from ‘A’ishah (RA), through al-Aswad; sahih); Sahih al-Bukhari 1538, 5918. Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 749: after bathing before ihram ‘A’ishah (RA) applied fragrance to the Prophet {{1}}, and its gleam could be seen even after ihram (sirah-based; this narration of Muslim and al-Bukhari is as a habit, the Farewell Hajj is not specifically mentioned).
footnotes.6: Sahih Muslim 1185 (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)); through Abu Zumayl. ‘Qad qad’ means ‘enough, stop’. The polytheists’ extra words ‘illa sharikan huwa lak tamlikuhu wa-ma malak’ (the idols were meant). The narration says they said these while circumambulating the Ka‘bah. The words of the Prophet’s {{1}} own talbiyah, and Jabir’s ‘he recited the talbiyah of tawhid’, are in Sahih Muslim 1218.
footnotes.7: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). The Bengali pronunciation of the talbiyah is the author’s; the Arabic text is exactly as in the narration.
footnotes.8: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). This part is Jabir’s own eyewitness account. No specific number of people is in the sahih narration; in al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 750 ‘one hundred and twenty-four thousand or one hundred and forty-four thousand’ has come (sirah-based, the chain not verified), so no number has been put in the narration.
footnotes.10: The words of the talbiyah: Sahih al-Bukhari 1549 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA): ‘the talbiyah of the Messenger of Allah {{1}}: labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa-al-ni‘mata laka wa-al-mulk, la sharika lak’). Extra words: in Jabir (RA)’s narration (Sahih Muslim 1218) people were adding ‘dhal ma‘arij’ and the like, the Prophet {{2}} did not turn them away and held to his own talbiyah. Ibn ‘Umar (RA) himself also used to add some words (Sahih Muslim 1184). It is better to stay with the words of the Sunnah; the fuqaha’ have discussion about extra words.
footnotes.11: Sunan Ibn Majah 2890 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)). Disagreement on the ruling: al-Albani said ‘sahih’ in Sahih Ibn Majah 2355 and ‘sahih li-ghayrihi’ in Sahih al-Targhib 1122; Ibn Hajar in Fath al-Bari 3/446 called the chain ‘weak’ (discussion of the narrators Rabi‘ ibn Sabih and Yazid ibn Aban). So here it has come only as a plain picture of mount and dress, not as evidence for any ruling. ‘Riya’’ = showing off, ‘sum‘ah’ = making people hear.
footnotes.12: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). The background of ramal is in the ‘Umrat al-Qada’ section of Dars 21. In the same narration: after the tawaf he came to Maqam Ibrahim and recited ‘wa-ttakhidhu min Maqami Ibrahima musalla’ (Surah al-Baqarah 2:125), the Maqam stayed between him and the Ka‘bah, and in the two rak‘ahs he recited Surah al-Ikhlas and Surah al-Kafirun.
footnotes.13: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). In the same narration also: after reciting the verse of Safa and Marwah (Surah al-Baqarah 2:158), saying ‘abda’u bi-ma bada’a Allahu bihi’ and beginning from Safa.
footnotes.14: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). In the same narration he also said, whoever has no sacrificial animal with him should undo ihram and make it an ‘umrah.
footnotes.15: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 749–750 (the command to the Companions who had no hady to change ihram for ‘umrah and become lawful; the Companions’ hesitation; the Prophet’s {{1}} statement ‘what has happened later, had I known earlier…’). The hesitation part is sirah-based, the chain has not been verified in this dars; ‘Suraqah’s question’ and the Prophet’s {{2}} command are in Sahih Muslim 1218.
footnotes.16: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju‘shum: that man who pursued the Prophet {{1}} on the road of hijrah, later became Muslim (came in Dars 11). Showing by interlacing the fingers: a sign of ‘umrah and Hajj becoming joined together.
footnotes.17: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA), narrating the saying of ‘Ali (RA); sahih). Wording of the narration: ‘fa-kana ‘Aliyyun yaqulu bi-al-‘Iraq…’ (‘Ali used to say in Iraq). ‘Ali’s arrival from Yemen and the number of the hady in the same narration.
footnotes.18: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). In the same narration: the animals brought by ‘Ali (RA) and those with the Prophet {{1}} together came to one hundred in all. The incident of ‘Ali’s Yemen expedition and Buraydah’s complaint is in a later part of the dars (the return road at Khumm).
footnotes.19: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). (The narration says ‘Yawm al-Tarwiyah’; that is 8 Dhu al-Hijjah.) Namirah: a place just outside the boundary of ‘Arafah.
footnotes.20: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). Explanation of the ‘Hums’ custom: Sahih al-Bukhari 4520, Sahih Muslim 1219 (from ‘A’ishah (RA)): Quraysh and the followers of their religion used to stop at Muzdalifah and call themselves ‘Hums’, the rest of the Arabs went to ‘Arafah; when Islam came Allah commanded His Prophet to go to ‘Arafah and return from there. Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, p. 123, note 133 (the same explanation).
footnotes.21: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, Surah al-Baqarah 2:199, p. 123 (matched by rendering the printed page and reading). Arabic: Al-Qur’an Cloud (Uthmani script). Occasion of revelation: Sahih al-Bukhari 4520; Sahih Muslim 1219 (from ‘A’ishah (RA)).
footnotes.22: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). In the sirah account the name of the place is ‘Batn ‘Uranah’ (al-Rahiq al-Makhtum, Bengali, p. 750).
footnotes.23: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 751 (Rabi‘ah ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf (RA) conveying the sentences in a loud voice; source: Ibn Hisham 2/605). The chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.
footnotes.24: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). ‘Ghayra mubarrih’ (not painful): the dictionary meaning of the word is ‘that which does not give pain or injury’. Another narration of the same address: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 1163 (from ‘Amr ibn al-Ahwas (RA); ‘hasan sahih’). Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 750–751 has the same statement too. In Dars 2 only the first sentence of this narration came (note 112).
footnotes.25: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 1163 (from ‘Amr ibn al-Ahwas (RA), through his son Sulayman; al-Tirmidhi: ‘hasan sahih’; al-Albani, Sahih al-Tirmidhi 1163: ‘hasan’). The word ‘‘awan’ is from ‘‘aniyyah’ (a captive); here the meaning is being sheltered and dependent in the husband’s hand (meaning of the word: dictionary-based). At the end of this narration come ‘leaving the bed’ and ‘a blow that is not painful’ in the case of indecency, which agree with Jabir (RA)’s narration (Muslim 1218).
footnotes.26: Sahih Muslim 2328 (from ‘A’ishah (RA); sahih). Al-Albani, Mukhtasar al-Shama’il 299: sahih; Arna’ut, Takhrij al-Musnad 25715: sahih.
footnotes.27: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). ‘Addayta’ = you fulfilled (the trust); ‘nasahta’ = you wished well. Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 751 (the same incident; through Muslim).

quiz.q: Counting on his fingers, of how many years did Jabir (RA) begin his account of the Farewell Hajj?
o: Eight years
Five years
Ten years
Nine years

quiz.q: After the Hajj under Abu Bakr (RA)’s leadership, what announcement did ‘Ali (RA) make at Mina?
o: Undoing ihram is now forbidden
After this Hajj no one will pay jizyah
After this year no polytheist will perform Hajj
The ‘Arafah address is cancelled

quiz.q: What was the real reason so many people rushed to the Farewell Hajj?
o: A huge political gathering of the leaders of all Arab tribes
A special invitation of the Quraysh leaders
The announcement of the distribution of Yemen’s spoils
Each wanted to see him and act as he acted

quiz.q: Who was the woman whose child was born at Dhu al-Hulayfah?
o: Umm Sulaym bint Milhan
‘A’ishah bint Abi Bakr
Fatimah bint Muhammad
Asma’ bint ‘Umays

quiz.q: When Asma’ (RA) asked after the child’s birth, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: Go calmly, go calmly, O people
Undo your ihram and make it an ‘umrah
Bathe, bind on a cloth, enter ihram
Do not undo ihram, I have the hady with me

quiz.q: A mother who has just given birth wonders whether she can take part in worship in this condition. What does the incident of Asma’ (RA) teach?
o: Ask a scholar; the Shari‘ah has kept an easy answer
Give up worship on her own without asking anything
Decide entirely by herself
There is no way except sitting at home

quiz.q: In Anas (RA)’s narration, on what mount did the Prophet ﷺ perform Hajj?
o: On the back of a newly decked camel
On a worn saddle
On horseback in military dress
Always on the back of a white mule
quiz.e: Sunan Ibn Majah 2890 (disagreement over the chain in the note).

quiz.q: Why was the picture of the worn saddle and the four-dirham cloak brought into the dars?
o: Because exactly this dress is obligatory in Hajj
Because he had no money
As a picture of the absence of showing off in worship
Because everyone then used such saddles
quiz.e: Ibn Majah 2890; note: disagreement over the chain.
